about: The evangelium of the formulary “20th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, there was a certain ruler whose son was ill at Capernaum. When this man heard that Jesus was coming from Judea into Galilee, he went to Him and was asking Him to come down and heal his son, for he was beginning to die. Then Jesus said to him: Unless you see signs and wonders, you do not believe. The ruler says to Him: Lord, come down before my son dies. Jesus says to him: Go, your son lives. The man believed the word which Jesus had spoken to him, and he was going on his way. And as he was already going down, servants came to meet him and brought word, saying that his son was living. So he was asking them the hour at which he had improved. And they said to him: Yesterday, at the seventh hour, the fever left him. The father then knew that it was that hour in which Jesus had said to him: Your son lives; and he himself believed, and his whole household.
